notes.tech: Thread proposed 1 (2026-10-11): water-repellent nylon (unbranded) on quilted jackets, gilet and windbreakers; UV-resistant nylon (Sounds coach jacket); recycled polyester (Checks windbreaker); "technical cotton" that is 100% polyester; Japanese denim (no mill named); no named membrane or insulation — NONE: no owned or licensed membrane, insulation or performance fibre named on any of 304 men's clothing PDPs; share of range 0 of 304 styles name an owned or licensed technology; 27 of 304 are synthetic-le. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.
notes.craft: Thread proposed 2 (2026-10-11): Kenzo states the country of making on every men's PDP (304 of 304, ten countries, Portugal and Tunisia leading) but names no maker, mill or owned factory, and documents no process beyond technique words in product bullets. The dated Paris heritage (1970, Galerie Vivienne) is real but is design heritage, not making. That is a 2: country stated, little else. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.

marks: water-repellent nylon (unbranded) on quilted jackets, gilet and windbreakers

craft_evidence.owned: claim only: LVMH maison page says the 18 rue Vivienne head office houses the studio, the workshop and product development; no factory claimed as owned; PDPs show garments made in 10 countries by unnamed suppliers
craft_evidence.makers: no: none of 304 men's clothing PDPs names a factory, workshop or maker
craft_evidence.mills: no: "Japanese denim" on the denim range and "Prince of Wales wool" on one jacket, but no cloth or yarn mill named on any PDP
craft_evidence.madein: 304 of 304 men's clothing PDPs state the country (Portugal 116, Tunisia 71, China 52, Romania 28, Turkey 11, Bulgaria 10, Moldova 6, Italy 5, Madagascar 3, Vietnam 2), all read 11 Oct
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: founded Paris 1970 by Kenzo Takada, first boutique in Galerie Vivienne (LVMH maison page); flagship at 3 Place des Victoires from 1976 (kenzo.com SS27 page)
craft_evidence.process: no: PDP bullets name techniques (intarsia, chainstitch embroidery, jacquard, dip dye) but the brand publishes no account of how or where its garments are made
craft_evidence.reasoning: Kenzo states the country of making on every men's PDP (304 of 304, ten countries, Portugal and Tunisia leading) but names no maker, mill or owned factory, and documents no process beyond technique words in product bullets. The dated Paris heritage (1970, Galerie Vivienne) is real but is design heritage, not making. That is a 2: country stated, little else.
